With this report explaining the actions it will take to reduce CO2 emissions, which are also what is causing the current climate crisis, Üsküdar Municipality has shown that it is highly concerned about social, environmental, and economic issues that the world is likely to suffer even more intensely as the crisis intensifies, and such issues are mainly projected as starvation, migration, disasters, and drought. Also, the report contains the values determined as BAU in the absence of these actions.
The so-called term 'Business as Usual' (BAU) scenario refers to a scenario in which normal conditions are anticipated to remain unchanged or in which there are no substantial changes to technology, the economy, or governmental practices. According to the report's predictions, Üsküdar will emit 1,538,870.05 tons of CO2 equivalent in 2021 and 2,079,384.65 tons in 2030. A 40% decrease from the base year level is the target for 2030, using base year emissions as a base.
Analysis show that the average temperature changes in the region, including Üsküdar will occur as an increase of 0.5°C in average temperature in the stabilization scenario and, additionally, a 1.25°C average temperature increase in the worst-case scenario that are projected in the period of 2041-2080 compared to the period of 2022-2040. The stabilization scenario shows a very slight increase in the period 2081-2098 compared to the prior period of 2041-2080, a worst-case increase of 1.25°C, and an increase of 2.5°C compared to the period 2022-2040.
One of the most significant findings in the report, which applies to Üsküdar, is that the increase, which is now near to 1°C, may sometimes reach up to 2°C and disproportionately reduce close to 2°C. The activities specified in the report should be performed in any case in the upcoming periods as this shifting pattern is often in the trend of rise.
In Üsküdar, the quantity of CO2 equivalent emissions falls from 2079.38 tons to 923.32 tons CO2 equivalent with a 40% reduction if nothing is changed, when compared to 2030 BAU with a 40% reduction from the base year in total emissions, whereas the quantity of CO2 equivalent emissions per person drops from 3.96 tons without any action to 1.76 tons CO2 equivalent per person in the comparison of the 2030 BAU also with a 40% reduction in total emissions from the base year.
As can be seen in the report, most of the action plans include activities that fall under the responsibility of the municipality or that the municipality is expected to coordinate; hence it clearly demonstrates that Üsküdar Municipality gives great importance on the process of implementing the actions put forward. In addition to that, Üsküdar Municipality places a great emphasis on ensuring that all stakeholders are involved in the process accordingly.

Thua Thien Hue province has a strategy for green procurement and purchase of goods and services, primarily as part of its broader initiatives on circular economy, green growth, and climate change adaptation. While there might not be a single document titled 'Green Procurement Strategy,' the province's actions and policies demonstrate a clear commitment to this principle.
Key Initiatives and Evidence
Circular Economy Action Plan: In July 2025, the province adopted Decision No. 284/KH-UBND, which outlines a plan for implementing the National Action Plan on a Circular Economy by 2035 in Hue City. This plan specifically mentions 'mainstream[ing] circular procurement' as a key intervention. This means the province is actively working to integrate the purchase of goods and services that minimize waste and maximize resource value into its official procurement processes.
Green Transportation and Public Services: Thua Thien Hue has implemented several projects to reduce emissions from public services. These include:
Piloting the use of electric vehicles for waste collection, with electric trucks now in use by the Hue Urban Environment and Public Works Joint Stock Company (HEPCO). This is a direct example of the government procuring low-emission vehicles for public services.
Providing preferential loans for individuals to purchase electric vehicles, a policy that indirectly influences the market toward greener goods.
Waste Reduction and Management: The province has a strong focus on reducing plastic waste, particularly in the tourism sector. This includes initiatives to promote 'green shopping' and discourage single-use plastics, which impacts the types of goods and services that businesses and the public purchase.
Integration with Broader Goals: The province's efforts are aligned with national strategies and the goal of becoming a 'green, smart, and environmentally friendly' city. By promoting green growth and sustainable development, the province inherently includes green procurement as a tool to achieve its larger environmental and economic objectives.
Additionally, broader provincial initiatives, like the Hue GrEEEn City Action Plan (supported by ADB) and climate adaptation projects (e.g., CARe Hue funded by the Green Climate Fund), reinforce these standards by emphasizing green public procurement in sectors like tourism, agriculture, and infrastructure. For instance, pilots for electric vehicles in waste collection and low-emission zones in tourist areas extend to procurement criteria for services and goods.
While no standalone 'emissions-only' procurement law exists at the provincial level, these elements form a cohesive strategy embedded in national and local planning, with ongoing implementation as of 2025.

While a specific, standalone strategy or standard document for reducing emissions from public procurement in Ca Mau Province is not publicly available, the province has integrated this objective into its broader environmental and economic planning. National directives guide Ca Mau, and the province has its own provincial action plan that mandates green public procurement.
National Guidance and Provincial Implementation
Vietnam's National Green Growth Strategy for the 2021-2030 period sets a clear direction for sustainable development, including specific targets for green public procurement. This national strategy serves as the foundational framework for all provinces, including Ca Mau.
In response, Ca Mau Province has developed and issued its own Green Growth Action Plan for the 2021-2030 period. This plan, enacted on December 14, 2023, outlines the province's commitment to greening its economic sectors and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
Green Public Procurement within the Action Plan
Within the framework of implementing the national strategy, the Ca Mau Provincial People's Committee has assigned specific responsibilities to its departments. Notably, the Department of Finance is tasked with the implementation of green public procurement and green public services for state agencies. This indicates a clear intention to incorporate environmental and emission reduction criteria into the province's procurement processes.
Although the full text of Ca Mau's provincial action plan is not widely accessible, its existence and the explicit assignment of green procurement responsibilities confirm that the province is actively pursuing measures to reduce the environmental impact of its procurement activities. This approach aligns with the national goals and reflects a commitment to sustainable development at the provincial level.
In summary, while Ca Mau Province may not have a distinct, publicly available document detailing a strategy for emission reduction in procurement, it has formally adopted this goal within its comprehensive Green Growth Action Plan, in line with the national strategy. The implementation of this is a designated responsibility of the provincial Department of Finance.

column16: Desde la Administración se realiza el análisis de significancia de los bienes y servicios (B&S) adquiridos dando un puntaje a las emisiones generadas por el consumo de B&S por medio de variables definidas (magnitud/ volumen de las emisiones , nivel de influencia en fuentes/ sumideros entre otras) con el fin de seleccionar las emisiones mas significativas que son generadas por los B&S consumidos por la administración.\nCon base en este ejercicio se crearon fichas técnicas para estos bienes priorizados, estableciendo criterios de sostenibilidad para la adquisición de los mismos, de esta manera adquirimos un porcentaje de las compras totales de la administración con criterios de sostenibilidad.
